status: proposal (ADR-0095); nothing is implemented; every rule has maturity proposed

verdicts.PASS: no finding at gating level, every prerequisite present, and no incomplete relation among the rule reads
verdicts.FAIL: at least one unsuppressed finding of level error (or warning in the release tier), and every incomplete relation the rule reads is read positively and directly (monotone: a seen finding is real on partial input)
verdicts.NOT_RUN: a prerequisite is missing, or an incomplete relation is read negatively or through a derived relation (whatever the rule found), or an incomplete positive read with no finding; absorbs PASS, never absorbs FAIL at fold level
verdicts.order: FAIL < NOT_RUN < PASS (chain minimum across independent rules)

categories.extraction: Extractor health: partial parses and missing prerequisites
categories.link-integrity: Dangling, stale, orphaned, duplicated and ill-typed links (the compile-time checks)
categories.traceability: Orphans and coverage: requirement, test, term, persona, journey, UI element
categories.language: Ubiquitous-language and naming drift against the term registry
categories.model-code: Model versus code: workflow, generated artefacts, formal models
categories.ui: UI versus domain model, API, tokens and evidence
categories.evidence: Evidence freshness, status-lattice violations and proof-claim discipline
categories.governance: Rules about rules: suppressions, baselines, catalogue, ledger, protected policy

kinds.file-local: Python function over one file's facts; cache unit is the file content hash
kinds.graph-global: SQL violation query (or Python over declared relations) over the canonical graph; zero rows means pass
kinds.template: Generated from a metamodel constraint (cardinality or acyclicity); no hand-written query
kinds.adapter: Findings computed by a pinned external tool and mapped to a WV id by an adapter table
kinds.rendered: Needs a rendered capture (one browser, serial); NOT_RUN without Chrome
kinds.harness: Computed by the determinism harness over whole runs, not over graph facts
kinds.test-level: A property or law test over an implementation, reported as a finding when it fails
kinds.meta: About the rule system itself (catalogue, fixtures, suppressions, ledger)

severities.warning: ratcheted in fast and full, blocks in release
severities.notrun: prerequisite missing; verdict NOT_RUN, blocks unless accepted

tiers.fast: stdlib Python only, seconds, every save and commit
tiers.full: adds harness, second process or browser, serial
tiers.release: double rebuild, external validators, POSIX compare

strata.0: base facts and non-recursive projections; positive rules only
strata.1: derived relations, or negation over base facts
strata.3: rules over the findings of other rules (suppression hygiene); run after strata 0 to 2 are materialised
strata.formula: stratum(rule) = max(0, max over positive reads of stratum(rel), max over negative reads of stratum(rel) + 1)

link_status.<kind>: node.<T> for each node type at an anchored end of <kind> (metamodel anchor_ends and signatures)

banned_apis.reason: unsorted directory order (D-09); use the sorted listing helper
randomness (D-04); a seeded generator needs an ADR-lite exception
component labels depend on insertion order (D-09)

rules.name: dangling-link
rules.statement: link(L, K, F, T, _, _), (not node(F) or not node(T)), not node_before(missing endpoint)

witness.detail: the link and the unresolved endpoint

messages.text: Link {link} ({kind}) points at {endpoint}, which is not in the graph and was not in the baseline.

rules.why: A link to an id that never existed cannot be checked; a broken link is an error, stricter than OKF, which tolerates it. Merges the ui-dangling-link (UIL-001), unresolved-term-binding and calls-to-missing-operation ideas: the kind is an argument, not a new rule.
rules.false_positive_control: exact; ids that existed at the baseline are reported by WV-004 with rename help instead, so one defect has one rule

rules.name: ill-typed-edge
rules.statement: link(L, K, F, T), type(F)=TF, type(T)=TT, not signature(K, TF, TT)

witness.detail: the link and the violated signature rows of its kind

messages.text: Link {link}: kind {kind} does not allow {from_type} -> {to_type}. Allowed: {allowed}.

rules.why: Many-sorted edge signatures make an ill-typed link fail at build time; the signatures are generated from the metamodel so an agent cannot widen one to make a link pass.
rules.false_positive_control: exact; supertypes are expanded by the metamodel builder, not by the rule

rules.name: duplicate-id
rules.statement: node(I, T1, H1, S1), node(I, T2, H2, S2), S1 != S2

witness.detail: the two definition sites

messages.text: Id {id} is defined at {site_a} and {site_b}; status AMBIGUOUS.

rules.why: Two definitions of one id make every link to it ambiguous; OpenFastTrace calls this state Ambiguous.
rules.false_positive_control: exact; the extractor emits one node per definition site

rules.name: orphaned-link
rules.statement: link(L, K, F, T), node_before(T), not node(T), not rename_map(T, _)

witness.detail: the link and the absent target

messages.text: Link {link} ({kind}) points at {target}, which existed at the baseline and is gone. Candidates: {candidates}.

rules.why: A moved or deleted target makes a link ORPHANED; measured on Doorstop history 20.6% of symbols are missing after 100 commits, so relocation help is worth having.
rules.false_positive_control: exact for the finding; the candidate list is advisory (same content hash, same fragment in another path) and never becomes a link

fix.what: propose a rename_map entry and a retargeted link; a human applies it

rules.name: suspect-link
rules.statement: link_status(L, SUSPECT, Direct or Transitive)

witness.detail: baseline digest, current digest and the path to the changed target

messages.text: Link {link}: target {target} changed since the baseline ({baseline_digest} -> {current_digest}); review, then a human acknowledges.
Link {link} depends through {path_length} hops on a changed target {target}.

rules.why: A changed normalised digest means the target changed since a human last accepted the link, not that the link is false. Early cutoff: a comment-only edit changes no digest, so nothing is suspect.
rules.false_positive_control: exact over the chosen hash method; the method-per-link-kind policy sets the noise level (symbol AST 7 to 9% per change, signature 1.5 to 1.8%, two Python repos)

fix.what: clearing is a human ledger act (ADR-0094); an agent may propose a review summary only

rules.name: unresolved-resolver
rules.statement: extractor_run(E, not_run, Reason)

witness.detail: the missing tool or grammar and its pin

messages.text: Extractor {extractor} did not run: {reason}. Every rule that reads {relations} reports NOT_RUN.

rules.why: A missing parser or tool must read as NOT_RUN and absorb PASS; it must never look green.
rules.false_positive_control: exact by construction: the finding is the absence of a prerequisite, reported once per extractor
rules.not_run_when: the reporter itself never reports NOT_RUN

rules.name: inferred-link-satisfies-gate
rules.statement: link(L, K, F, T, _, _, inferred), counts_toward_gate(K)

witness.detail: the inferred link found in a coverage numerator

messages.text: Link {link} has class inferred (tool {tool}) but is counted toward {gate}; inferred links are proposals.

rules.why: LLM or IR recovered links reach F1 of about 0.8 at best (2025 study); they must never satisfy a gate until a human promotes them to a declared link.
rules.false_positive_control: exact; the class field is written by the extractor and checked by the schema

rules.name: id-removed-without-rename-map
rules.statement: node_before(I), not node(I), not rename_map(I, _)

witness.detail: the removed id

messages.text: Id {id} existed at the baseline, is gone and has no rename_map entry.

rules.why: Identity is by id, never by label; a rename must be an explicit record so links and OKF pages survive it (D-23).
rules.false_positive_control: exact; deleting a node on purpose needs a rename_map entry with new id null and a reason

fix.what: propose a rename_map entry with the new id left blank

rules.name: partial-extraction-gated
rules.statement: partial_fact(File, Position)

witness.detail: file and parse-error position

messages.text: {file} does not parse ({position}); stdlib ast raised SyntaxError.
{file} was parsed with error recovery ({position}); facts from it are labelled partial and cannot PASS.

rules.why: A partial parse loses definitions silently (tree-sitter recovered class A and lost f and g in the dossier probe); labelling it stops a green result on incomplete facts (D-14).
rules.false_positive_control: Python syntax errors are exact (stdlib ast); tree-sitter recovery is labelled partial and reported as NOT_RUN, never as an error about the source

rules.name: requirement-without-verifier
rules.statement: node.requirement(N), count(covered_link of kind verifies, incoming, N) < 1

witness.detail: the closed-world scope: node, link kind, side, the links seen and their statuses

messages.text: Requirement {node} has {count} covered verifies links (needs {min}). Scope searched: {links_seen}.

rules.why: Every requirement needs a verifier (test, property, model check or witness). Only COVERED links count, so a requirement whose only verifier is SUSPECT or ORPHANED is reported here and the link rules explain why.
rules.false_positive_control: exact over declared links; coverage says a test is linked, not that it would catch a fault (mutation lane calibrates)

rules.name: requirement-without-satisfier
rules.statement: node.requirement(N), count(covered_link of kind satisfies, incoming, N) < 1

witness.detail: the closed-world scope: node, link kind, side, the links seen and their statuses

messages.text: Requirement {node} has {count} covered satisfies links (needs {min}). Scope searched: {links_seen}.

rules.why: Every requirement needs something that satisfies it (symbol, workflow element, UI control, component or contract).
rules.false_positive_control: exact over declared links

rules.name: symbol-without-requirement
rules.statement: node.symbol(S), in_policy_scope(S), no covered satisfies or names link from S

witness.detail: closed-world scope searched: the satisfies and names links seen for the symbol

messages.text: Public symbol {symbol} has no covered satisfies or names link. Scope searched: {links_seen}.

rules.why: Completeness matters as much as rot: about 60% of commits carry issue links in the literature (Rath 2018). Report-only until the policy scope is calibrated.
rules.false_positive_control: policy-limited: only symbols in the declared public scope (domain and application) count

rules.name: unwanted-coverage
rules.statement: link(L, K, F, T), target_needs_no_coverage(T, policy)

witness.detail: the covering link

messages.text: Link {link} covers {target}, which the coverage policy exempts (status UNWANTED).

rules.why: Coverage of something that needs none is noise; OpenFastTrace calls it Unwanted. Needs a policy of which items require coverage.
rules.false_positive_control: exact given the policy; the policy is protected (WV-095)

rules.name: single-point-of-evidence
rules.statement: d dominates every path from requirement R to its covered evidence

witness.detail: the dominator node and the paths that pass through it

messages.text: All evidence for {requirement} passes through {dominator} ({paths} paths).

rules.why: Dominators on requirement-to-evidence paths expose evidence that fails together (Cooper, Harvey and Kennedy iterative dominators).
rules.false_positive_control: exact given the graph; a report, never a gate

rules.name: redundant-link
rules.statement: link(L, K, F, T) is implied by a path F -> ... -> T of other links of kind K (transitive reduction on the condensation)

witness.detail: the alternate path

messages.text: Link {link} is implied by {alternate}.

rules.why: Redundant links add review cost and stale noise; transitive reduction is unique on a DAG.
rules.false_positive_control: exact on the condensation; reduction is not unique with cycles, so cycles are collapsed first

rules.name: evidence-redundancy-below-k
rules.statement: min vertex cut between requirement R and its covered evidence is < k

witness.detail: the canonical minimum vertex cut (source-side minimal)

messages.text: Requirement {requirement} has redundancy {redundancy} (< {k}); cut {cut}.

rules.why: Redundancy k says how many independent nodes must fail before evidence is lost.
rules.false_positive_control: min cuts are not unique, so the cut is canonicalised; a report, never a gate

rules.name: homonym-in-context
rules.statement: term_form(T1, C, F, preferred), term_form(T2, C, F, preferred), T1 != T2

witness.detail: the form and the two concepts

messages.text: Preferred form {form} names two terms in context {context}: {term_a} and {term_b}.

rules.why: Deissenboeck and Pizka: a name with two concepts is a homonym; the naming system is consistent only if the relation is a bijection.
rules.false_positive_control: exact set check on registry data; no NLP

rules.name: synonym-two-preferred-forms
rules.statement: term_form(T, C, F1, preferred), term_form(T, C, F2, preferred), F1 != F2

witness.detail: the concept and its two preferred forms

messages.text: Term {term} has two preferred forms in context {context}: {form_a} and {form_b}.

rules.why: A concept with two preferred names splits the language; the second name should be an accepted form.
rules.false_positive_control: exact set check

rules.name: form-shared-by-two-terms
rules.statement: term_form(T1, C, F, K1), term_form(T2, C, F, K2), T1 != T2, not (K1 = preferred and K2 = preferred)

witness.detail: the form and the two terms

messages.text: Form {form} (classes {class_a} and {class_b}) belongs to terms {term_a} and {term_b} in context {context}; matching it is ambiguous.

rules.why: An accepted or hidden form shared by two terms makes surface matching ambiguous; the preferred-preferred case is WV-017.
rules.false_positive_control: exact set check

rules.name: forbidden-form-at-declaration
rules.statement: identifier(Site, Words), term_form(T, C, F, forbidden, ReplacedBy), F is a contiguous word sequence of Words

witness.detail: the declaration site and replaced_by

messages.text: {site} declares {name}, which contains forbidden form {form}; use {replaced_by} (term {term}).

rules.why: Exact-token matching after a pinned splitter, at declaration sites only, is the low-false-positive part of vocabulary enforcement; ML consistency models reach 67.9% F1 and stay advisory.
rules.false_positive_control: declaration sites only, ASCII code-facing forms, pinned splitter; unsplittable names are counted in unknown_names, never guessed

fix.what: LibCST rename proposal with a rename_map entry (phase 3)

rules.not_run_when: unsplittable names are reported as a count, not NOT_RUN

rules.name: acyclic-link-cycle
rules.statement: scc.K has a component of size > 1 (or a self loop) for a link kind K declared acyclic

witness.detail: the cycle, members sorted, relabelled by minimum member

messages.text: Link kind {kind} must be acyclic but {members} form a cycle: {cycle}.

rules.why: contains, derived_from, refines, renamed_to and supersedes are declared acyclic in the metamodel. Generalises the brief's cyclic-broader idea (WV-022, terms only) to every acyclic kind, so ADR supersession cycles and requirement refinement cycles need no rule of their own.
rules.false_positive_control: exact; SCC labels use minimum-member relabelling so the cycle report is order independent (24 forms over 200 shuffles for nx.condensation, 1 for sorted SCC, MEASUREMENT)

rules.name: deprecated-without-replaced-by
rules.statement: term_meta(T, status=deprecated), no replaced_by

witness.detail: the term

messages.text: Term {term} is deprecated and names no replacement.

rules.why: A deprecated term without a replacement leaves every user of it without an instruction.
rules.false_positive_control: exact

rules.name: unbound-identifier-report
rules.statement: identifier(Site, Name, Freq), high frequency, not named by any names link

witness.detail: the identifier and its frequency

messages.text: Identifier word {word} occurs {frequency} times and names no term; glossary candidate.

rules.why: In this repo only 3 of 10 glossary terms appear as contiguous identifier words (MEASUREMENT), and words such as candidate (22) and proposal (26) are not terms; the report feeds the glossary, never a failure.
rules.false_positive_control: report only; never gates

rules.name: import-cycle
rules.statement: scc.depends_on has a component of size > 1

witness.detail: the SCC members sorted, relabelled by minimum member

messages.text: Modules {members} form a dependency cycle of {size}.

rules.why: Cycles are real in this graph; collapse each SCC before any DAG algorithm and report every cycle deterministically. Imports found statically are a may-edge: dynamic imports are invisible.
rules.false_positive_control: over-approximate edges may include imports guarded by TYPE_CHECKING; those carry a qualifier and are excluded by the extractor

rules.name: architecture-reflexion
rules.statement: component_edge(A, B) not allowed by allow_decl (divergence), or allow_decl(A, B) with no component_edge (absence)

witness.detail: the offending component edge with the module edges that induce it

messages.text: Components {from_component} -> {to_component} depend on each other via {via}, which the intended architecture does not allow (divergence).
The intended architecture allows {from_component} -> {to_component} but no module edge realises it (absence).

rules.why: Reflexion models (Murphy, Notkin, Sullivan) compare the intended architecture with the extracted one: convergence, divergence, absence.
rules.false_positive_control: the extracted edge is a may-edge; divergences carry the inducing module edges so a reviewer can judge

rules.name: diagram-semantic-hash-drift
rules.statement: diagram_meta(D, Embedded), projection_hash(source(D)) != Embedded

witness.detail: the embedded hash and the recomputed projection hash

messages.text: Diagram {diagram} embeds hash {embedded} but its source projects to {recomputed}; regenerate it.

rules.why: Every generated view embeds the hash of the source it was projected from (visual ADR-0023); drift is a hash comparison, never a judgement (ProofMap GAP-030).
rules.false_positive_control: exact; the cheap check that needs no generator run (WV-065 is the full one)

rules.name: view-mapping-totality
rules.statement: semantic_type(T), not in view_mapping as drawn or not_shown

witness.detail: the semantic type with no entry

messages.text: Semantic type {type} has no entry in view mapping {view}: it is neither drawn nor marked not_shown.

rules.why: One of the two category-theory checks we adopt: a new semantic type cannot silently vanish from a view.
rules.false_positive_control: exact

rules.name: lens-law-violation
rules.statement: an edit sequence e on a view violates GetPut, PutGet (mod layout and declared amendments) or conditional PutPut

witness.detail: the minimal counterexample edit and the base

messages.text: View {view}: law {law} fails for edit {edit} on base {base}.

rules.why: Views are asymmetric lenses; the laws are property tests over the tested alphabet, labelled MEASUREMENT on that alphabet, not a proof.
rules.false_positive_control: results are reported for the tested alphabet only

rules.name: uncovered-domain-action
rules.statement: node.transition(N), count(covered_link of kind realises, incoming from node.ui_control, N) < 1

witness.detail: the closed-world scope: node, link kind, side, the links seen and their statuses

messages.text: Transition {node} has no UI control that realises it. Scope searched: {links_seen}.

rules.why: A transition that a role can invoke needs a UI control that realises it (UIL-002); today the UI hard-codes 5 actions against a 4-action baseline (MEASUREMENT, static read). Distinct from WV-063: this rule counts only UI-control realisers, WV-063 only symbols, so a transition with code and no control fires this rule alone.
rules.false_positive_control: exact over the sidecar UI model; static tier sees only static controls and says so

rules.name: orphan-or-unkeyed-element
rules.statement: rendered element with an interactive role, no data-eija-key, or a key that is not in the sidecar

witness.detail: the element and the missing key

messages.text: Rendered {role} {name} has no key or key {key} is not in the UI model.

rules.why: UIL-003: interactive elements need a stable key so links survive restyling.
rules.false_positive_control: complete only over the captured states; one browser, serial
rules.not_run_when: Chrome or the capture is unavailable

rules.name: label-drift
rules.statement: rendered accessible name of a control that names term T is not a registered form of T

witness.detail: the accessible name and the registered forms

messages.text: Control {key} has accessible name {name}; term {term} allows {forms}.

rules.why: UIL-004: the browser computes the accessible name that a person and an assistive tool perceive, so this checks the UI as perceived, not as parsed.
rules.false_positive_control: exact for the captured states
rules.not_run_when: Chrome or the capture is unavailable

rules.name: enabledness-mismatch
rules.statement: for (state, actor): enabled(UI) != allowed(kernel)

witness.detail: the (state, actor) pair and the symmetric difference

messages.text: In state {state} for {actor} the UI enables {ui_only} but the kernel does not, and the kernel allows {kernel_only} but the UI does not.

rules.why: UIL-005: baseline drift measured statically (5 hard-coded actions against 4); complete only over the enumerated pairs, a bounded conformance check and not a proof about the UI.
rules.false_positive_control: MEASUREMENT over the enumerated pairs, with the enumeration size printed
rules.not_run_when: Chrome or the capture is unavailable

rules.name: token-drift
rules.statement: css var(--x) with no token, unused token, or raw colour literal

witness.detail: the css location and token

messages.text: {file} uses var(--{token}) but no design token defines it.
Design token {token} is used nowhere.
{file} uses raw colour {value}; use a design token.

rules.why: UIL-007: tokens decouple meaning from paint; a raw colour or an unknown variable is drift.
rules.false_positive_control: exact for static CSS

rules.name: ui-control-without-evidence
rules.statement: node.ui_control(N), count(covered_link of kind exercised_by, outgoing, N) < 1

witness.detail: the closed-world scope: node, link kind, side, the links seen and their statuses

messages.text: UI control {node} is exercised by {count} covered tests or journeys (needs {min}).

rules.why: A UI control no test or journey exercises has no evidence (UIL-008).
rules.false_positive_control: exact over links; the test reference is the data-eija-key in the test source

rules.name: statement-digest-mismatch
rules.statement: node.formal_law(L, D), approved_digest(L, A), D != A

witness.detail: the current digest against the owner-approved digest

messages.text: Statement {law} has digest {current} but the owner approved {approved}; a weaker statement can pass unnoticed.

rules.why: Statement pinning targets the weakened-postcondition attack: a proof of a different, weaker statement is not the proof that was asked for.
rules.false_positive_control: exact; the approved digest lives in the ledger, which only humans append

fix.what: clearing is a human ledger act (ADR-0094); an agent may propose a review summary only

rules.name: assumption-ledger-diff
rules.statement: assumption in a witness report not listed in the committed ledger

witness.detail: the unlisted assumption

messages.text: Witness {witness} rests on {assumption}, which the assumption ledger does not list.

rules.why: Bend unsafe, Lean sorryAx, Dafny axiom, cvc5 hole and TLA+ ASSUME each weaken a proof; an unlisted one is FAIL, a listed one makes the PASS say with assumptions.
rules.false_positive_control: exact given the tool's report
rules.not_run_when: the proof tool's report is unavailable

rules.name: proof-without-negative-control
rules.statement: models(FM, W) with proof evidence, no seeded-unsafe control that fails and no reachability witness

witness.detail: the model link and the controls searched

messages.text: Model {model} has a proof but no negative control or reachability witness.

rules.why: Vericoding studies show trivial solutions on weak specifications; a seeded-unsafe model that must FAIL catches a vacuous proof.
rules.false_positive_control: exact

rules.name: model-proof-worded-as-code
rules.statement: claim about code supported only by a proof link with no conforms_to

witness.detail: the claim, its supports and the missing conformance link

messages.text: Claim {claim} is about code but only model proof {witness} supports it.

rules.why: A proof about a model is not a proof about the code; wording a model proof as code correctness is the classic overclaim.
rules.false_positive_control: exact; depends on claims carrying a scope of code or model

rules.name: claim-graph-structure
rules.statement: claim-to-claim support edge, a cycle among claims, or a defeater with no resolution

witness.detail: the offending edge, the cycle or the unresolved defeater

messages.text: Claim graph: {problem} at {claim}.

rules.why: Assurance 2.0 structural rules: claims do not link directly to claims, the case is acyclic, an unresolved defeater blocks its parent.
rules.false_positive_control: exact

rules.name: non-canonical-committed-artefact
rules.statement: committed_file(F, Bytes), canonical(parse(Bytes)) != Bytes

witness.detail: the first differing byte after the canonical round trip

messages.text: {file} is not in canonical form (first difference at byte {offset}); floats and unsorted keys are not allowed (D-02, D-10).

rules.why: Committed graph artefacts use the RFC 8785 subset (strings, safe integers, booleans, null); the kernel's canonical() is not JCS for floats, -0.0, integers above 2^53 and astral key order (MEASUREMENT).
rules.false_positive_control: exact; conformance is tested against the RFC 8785 vectors

rules.name: nondeterminism-token-in-artefact
rules.statement: committed_file contains a timestamp, GUID, hostname or random token

witness.detail: the token and its offset

messages.text: {file} contains {token_kind} at byte {offset}; artefacts must not embed time, GUIDs or hosts (D-04).

rules.why: ProofMap GAP-003: regenerated timestamps churned files; the doctrine forbids wall clock in artefacts. Absolute paths moved to WV-082 so one defect has one rule.
rules.false_positive_control: pattern set is closed and versioned (ISO-8601 instants, UUID shapes, hostnames); heuristic on prose fields, exact on generated fields

rules.name: suppression-without-evidence-or-matching-nothing
rules.statement: suppression(S, Fp, Rule, Justification, Evidence), no evidence path that resolves, or no current finding with fingerprint Fp

witness.detail: the suppression id

messages.text: Suppression {id} for {rule} has no justification or its evidence path {evidence} does not resolve.
Suppression {id} matches no finding; delete it.

rules.why: ProofMap GAP-017/018: warnings accepted only with an id, a reason and an evidence path that resolves; import-linter reports an unmatched ignore as an error by default.
rules.false_positive_control: exact

rules.name: baseline-growth
rules.statement: baseline(Fp), not baseline_before(Fp)

witness.detail: the added baselined finding

messages.text: Baseline gained {fingerprint} ({rule}); baselines may shrink, never grow.

rules.why: Ratchet: existing debt is named, new debt cannot enter (ArchUnit freezing rules, quality-lane ratchet).
rules.false_positive_control: exact given the baseline ref

rules.name: hash-method-unregistered-or-mismatched
rules.statement: link(L, K, _, _, M, _), (not hash_method(M) or not hash_method_policy(K, M))

witness.detail: the link and its method name

messages.text: Link {link} ({kind}) uses hash method {method}: {problem}.

rules.why: A digest is meaningless without a registered, versioned method; policy per link kind stops a file digest on a requirement link, which would be stale on 99.9 to 100% of changes.
rules.false_positive_control: exact; the registry and policy are data reviewed with the okf lane

rules.name: obligation-reduced
rules.statement: obligation_before(O), not obligation(O), no ledger decision covering O

witness.detail: the removed or weakened obligation with its old and new value

messages.text: Obligation {obligation} ({kind}) held at the baseline ({old}) and no longer does ({new}); no ledger decision covers the change.

rules.why: Coverage rises when the set of requirements shrinks, so deleting or weakening a requirement, lowering a rule severity or disabling a rule can make a gate green without evidence; the moved-goalpost guard (agents aspect, section 8.3) is a rule over the graph and so also fires on free-form edits, not only on MCP proposals. Suppression additions are covered by WV-098 because suppressions.json is protected.
rules.false_positive_control: exact set difference over owner-owned obligation kinds (requirement and invariant statement digests, rule severity and maturity, acceptance rows); an owner ledger decision naming the obligation and its new digest covers it

fix.what: clearing is a human ledger act (ADR-0094); an agent may propose a review summary only

rules.name: same-author-evidence
rules.statement: requirement R, verifier V and satisfier S all authored_in_run(Run), no owner-approved statement digest for R

witness.detail: the requirement, its verifier and satisfier and the run that introduced all three

messages.text: Requirement {requirement}, verifier {verifier} and satisfier {satisfier} were all introduced by run {run} and no owner approved the statement; the author of a claim is weak evidence for it.

rules.why: An agent that writes the requirement, the test and the code has marked its own homework; the flag is advisory unless policy makes it blocking (agents aspect check C6).
rules.false_positive_control: provenance is observed at tool-call granularity only, so the rule may miss authorship (soundness may); it never claims the evidence is false

rules.name: ui-element-without-term
rules.statement: node.ui_control(N), count(covered_link of kind names, outgoing, N) < 1

witness.detail: the closed-world scope: node, link kind, side, the links seen and their statuses

messages.text: UI element {node} names {count} terms (needs {min}).

rules.why: A UI control, field, status or table that names no term shows vocabulary that the ubiquitous language does not own (orphan: UI element without domain term).
rules.false_positive_control: exact over declared names links; controls that show no domain vocabulary are exempt via coverage_policy
rules.metamodel: proposed to the metamodel lane (names obligation, out side, on ui_control, ui_field, ui_status, ui_table)

rules.name: persona-without-journey
rules.statement: node.persona(N), count(covered_link of kind serves, incoming, N) < 1

witness.detail: the closed-world scope: node, link kind, side, the links seen and their statuses

messages.text: Persona {node} is served by {count} journeys or requirements (needs {min}).

rules.why: A persona that no journey or requirement serves has no place in the product yet.
rules.false_positive_control: exact
rules.metamodel: proposed to the metamodel lane (serves obligation on persona)

rules.name: journey-without-persona
rules.statement: node.journey(N), count(covered_link of kind serves, outgoing, N) < 1

witness.detail: the closed-world scope: node, link kind, side, the links seen and their statuses

messages.text: Journey {node} serves {count} personas (needs {min}).

rules.why: A journey with no persona has no user; humans cannot review whose problem it solves.
rules.false_positive_control: exact
rules.metamodel: proposed to the metamodel lane (serves obligation, out side, on journey)

rules.name: term-without-bounded-context
rules.statement: node.term(N), count(covered_link of kind contains, incoming, N) < 1

witness.detail: the closed-world scope: node, link kind, side, the links seen and their statuses

messages.text: Term {node} is contained by {count} bounded contexts (needs {min}).

rules.why: A term belongs to exactly one bounded context (the DDD scope key); without it the homonym and synonym checks have no scope.
rules.false_positive_control: exact; the maximum of one is enforced by WV-055

rules.name: aggregate-term-without-realiser
rules.statement: node.term(N), count(covered_link of kind realises, incoming, N) < 1

witness.detail: the closed-world scope: node, link kind, side, the links seen and their statuses

messages.text: Aggregate term {node} is realised by {count} symbols (needs {min}).

rules.why: A term with ddd_role aggregate should be realised by at least one symbol, or the ubiquitous language names something the code does not have.
rules.false_positive_control: exact over declared realises links; applies only to terms with ddd_role aggregate

rules.name: link-cardinality-exceeded
rules.statement: count(links of kind K on side S of node N) > max declared by the metamodel signature

witness.detail: the node, the kind, the side and the links counted

messages.text: Node {node} has {count} {side} links of kind {kind}; the metamodel allows at most {max}.

rules.why: Functional constraints (a module belongs to one component, a transition has one source state) are declared once in the metamodel and checked by one generated rule.
rules.false_positive_control: exact; the generated query counts only links with status other than ORPHANED so a dangling link is not double counted

rules.name: term-without-binding
rules.statement: node.term(N), count(covered_link of kind names, incoming, N) < 1

witness.detail: the closed-world scope: node, link kind, side, the links seen and their statuses

messages.text: Term {node} is named by {count} covered links (needs {min}).

rules.why: A registry term that no symbol, UI element, document or test names is either dead vocabulary or an unbound one; either way the language and the code disagree (orphan: term without code).
rules.false_positive_control: exact; deprecated terms are excluded by the query
rules.metamodel: proposed to the metamodel lane (names obligation on term)

rules.name: layer-inversion
rules.statement: edge(A, B) in depends_on, calls, exposes with rank(component_of(A)) < rank(component_of(B))

witness.detail: the edge and the two layer ranks

messages.text: {source} (layer {source_layer}) depends on {target} (layer {target_layer}); lower layers must not depend on higher ones.

rules.why: import-linter checks Python imports; this rule covers every non-import edge kind as well (a UI control calling the domain directly), from the same declared layers.
rules.false_positive_control: may-edges; the declared layers are protected policy

rules.name: forbidden-component-dependency
rules.statement: component_edge(A, B), forbid_decl(A, B)

witness.detail: the forbidden edge and the inducing module edges

messages.text: Component {from_component} must not depend on {to_component}, but {via} does.

rules.why: Independence contracts (vendor-free domain, adapters wired only by bootstrap) stated once and checked over every edge kind.
rules.false_positive_control: may-edges; inducing edges shown

rules.name: module-without-component
rules.statement: node.module(N), count(covered_link of kind contains, incoming, N) < 1

witness.detail: the closed-world scope: node, link kind, side, the links seen and their statuses

messages.text: Module {node} is contained by {count} components (needs {min}).

rules.why: Every module belongs to a component of the intended architecture, else the reflexion model has a hole (the missing set of Murphy, Notkin and Sullivan).
rules.false_positive_control: exact; the maximum of one is enforced by WV-055
rules.metamodel: proposed to the metamodel lane (contains obligation, in side, component to module)

rules.name: diagram-element-unbound
rules.statement: diagram_element(E), derived_from(E, S), not node(S)

witness.detail: the diagram element and the missing model id

messages.text: Diagram element {element} claims to project {source}, which is not in the model.

rules.why: A diagram that shows something the model does not have misleads reviewers.
rules.false_positive_control: exact

rules.name: model-element-not-drawn
rules.statement: node.workflow_element(N), not drawn in view V, not declared not_shown in V

witness.detail: the view and the elements it draws

messages.text: Workflow element {element} appears in no diagram of view {view} and is not marked not_shown.

rules.why: The instance-level companion of totality (WV-028): a state or transition that no diagram shows is invisible to reviewers.
rules.false_positive_control: exact

rules.name: view-overlap-disagreement
rules.statement: view_fact(V1, Id, P, X1), view_fact(V2, Id, P, X2), V1 != V2, X1 != X2

witness.detail: the id, the property and the two views' values

messages.text: Views {view_a} and {view_b} disagree on {property} of {id}: {value_a} versus {value_b}.

rules.why: Views that share an id must agree on the shared facts (the overlap join, the implementable residue of sheaf-style consistency).
rules.false_positive_control: exact; only declared shared properties are compared

rules.name: workflow-element-without-realiser
rules.statement: node.transition(N), count(covered_link of kind realises, incoming from node.symbol, N) < 1

witness.detail: the closed-world scope: node, link kind, side, the links seen and their statuses

messages.text: Transition {node} is realised by {count} symbols (needs {min}).

rules.why: A workflow transition that no symbol realises is a model element with no code (model versus code). Guards and effects follow when their realises signature is added. Distinct from WV-031: this rule counts only symbol realisers, WV-031 only UI controls; the template parameter peer makes the two generated queries different.
rules.false_positive_control: exact over declared realises links; the extractor cannot infer realisation, it is declared
rules.metamodel: proposed to the metamodel lane (realises obligation, in side, symbol to transition)

rules.name: transition-not-exposed
rules.statement: node.transition(T), not exposed_transition(T)

witness.detail: the realising symbols and the operations they expose

messages.text: Transition {transition} is realised by no symbol that exposes an API operation; no client can invoke it.

rules.why: Closes the chain model, code, API: every transition should be reachable through an operation the UI can call.
rules.false_positive_control: exact over declared and derived links

rules.name: generated-artefact-drift
rules.statement: derived_from(A, S) generated, regenerated(A) != digest(A)

witness.detail: the artefact digest, the fresh digest and the first differing byte

messages.text: {artefact} differs from a fresh run of {generator} (first difference at byte {offset}).

rules.why: The GENERATED label is checked by re-running the pinned generator and comparing bytes; hand edits to generated files are rejected, not merged.
rules.false_positive_control: exact given a deterministic generator; a generator that is not byte-deterministic is itself a WV-087 style finding

rules.name: model-without-conformance-link
rules.statement: models(FM, W), no conforms_to(Code, FM)

witness.detail: the model and the absent conformance links

messages.text: Formal model {model} models {element} but no code conforms to it; its results are claims about the model only.

rules.why: A proof about a model is not a proof about the code; conformance is its own link with its own status. This rule keeps the boundary visible.
rules.false_positive_control: exact; informational, never a gate

rules.name: formal-law-without-formalises
rules.statement: node.formal_law(L), no formalises(L, Invariant or Requirement)

witness.detail: the law and the absent formalises links

messages.text: Formal law {law} formalises no invariant or requirement; nobody can say what it is a law of.

rules.why: A law that no requirement mentions may be vacuous; the human-reviewed fidelity link is the weak point of formal verification (spec soundness and completeness 52.3% for o3 on Verina).
rules.false_positive_control: exact

rules.name: evidence-subject-stale
rules.statement: evidence_subject(E, Dim, D1), current_subject(E, Dim, D2), D1 != D2

witness.detail: the changed subject dimension with both digests

messages.text: Evidence {evidence} is stale: subject dimension {dimension} changed ({recorded} -> {current}). Status STALE, not FAIL.

rules.why: Evidence is about a subject; when the semantic, implementation, policy, environment or harness digest moves, the evidence no longer speaks for the current tree.
rules.false_positive_control: exact; STALE means re-run, never that the claim is false

rules.name: checker-not-pinned
rules.statement: checked_by(E, Tool), not registered with a pinned version and sha256

witness.detail: the evidence and the unpinned tool

messages.text: Evidence {evidence} names checker {tool}, which has no pinned version and sha256 in the checker registry.

rules.why: A checker that is not pinned cannot be re-run to the same result; the registry (id, version, sha256, licence, sentinel) follows the tla lane's TOOLS.lock pattern.
rules.false_positive_control: exact

rules.name: supplied-status-mismatch
rules.statement: supplied_status(E, S1), evidence_verdict(E, S2), S1 != S2

witness.detail: the supplied and the recomputed verdict

messages.text: {artefact} says {supplied} but recomputation gives {recomputed}; supplied statuses are never trusted.

rules.why: The checker recomputes every verdict from raw observations (assess_link mirrors assess_receipt); a green field that nobody recomputed is not evidence.
rules.false_positive_control: exact

rules.name: not-run-absorbed-as-pass
rules.statement: aggregate_report(A, Inputs, Reported), NOT_RUN in Inputs, Reported = PASS

witness.detail: the aggregate and the NOT_RUN input

messages.text: Aggregate {aggregate} reports PASS although input {input} is NOT_RUN.

rules.why: NOT_RUN absorbs PASS in every aggregation, so order, threads and sharding cannot turn a skipped gate green.
rules.false_positive_control: exact

rules.name: conflicting-evidence
rules.statement: two evidence items on one claim with verdicts PASS and FAIL (join = CONFLICT)

witness.detail: the claim and the two conflicting items

messages.text: Claim {claim} has PASS from {evidence_a} and FAIL from {evidence_b}; status CONFLICT.

rules.why: The status join surfaces contradictory evidence instead of averaging it away; the kernel's aggregate_status agrees with the join on flat inputs up to length 6 (MEASUREMENT).
rules.false_positive_control: exact

rules.name: pass-without-tcb-label
rules.statement: evidence_verdict(E, PASS), label(E) missing or stronger than the checker kind allows

witness.detail: the evidence and its label

messages.text: Evidence {evidence} is PASS with label {label}; kind {kind} allows at most {allowed}.

rules.why: Every PASS prints its trusted computing base and label (GENERATED, PROVED_IN_MODEL, CHECKED_BOUNDED, TESTED, DECIDED); Z3 alone is SOLVER_TRUSTED, not PROVED.
rules.false_positive_control: exact against the label table per checker kind

rules.name: mocked-evidence-labelled-live
rules.statement: evidence_meta(E, mode=mocked or synthetic), claimed live

witness.detail: the evidence and the claim

messages.text: Evidence {evidence} was produced in mode {mode} but is presented as {claimed}.

rules.why: AGENTS.md: never claim a mocked provider was live or a synthetic test measured a human.
rules.false_positive_control: exact

rules.name: ledger-entry-dangling
rules.statement: ledger(Seq, Actor, Subject, Digest, Action), not node(Subject)

witness.detail: the ledger entry and the missing subject

messages.text: Ledger entry {seq} acts on {subject}, which is not in the graph.

rules.why: An acknowledgement of something that no longer exists is noise or an error in the decision plane.
rules.false_positive_control: exact

rules.name: adr-supersession-asymmetric
rules.statement: adr_meta(A, superseded_by, B) without supersedes(B, A), or supersedes(B, A) without the header on A

witness.detail: the header and the link

messages.text: ADR {adr} header says superseded by {other} but link supersedes {other} -> {adr} is missing (or the reverse).

rules.why: An ADR is never rewritten after acceptance; it is superseded by a new one, and both sides must say so.
rules.false_positive_control: exact

rules.name: superseded-adr-still-live
rules.statement: motivates(A, T), all motivators of T are superseded, no live motivator

witness.detail: the requirement, its superseded ADRs and their successors

messages.text: {target} is motivated only by superseded ADRs {superseded}; successors: {successors}.

rules.why: A requirement whose only rationale was replaced needs its motivation re-stated or re-linked.
rules.false_positive_control: exact

rules.name: adr-status-invalid
rules.statement: status not in {proposed, accepted, superseded by ADR-NNNN}

witness.detail: the ADR and its status line

messages.text: ADR {adr} has status {status}; allowed: proposed, accepted, superseded by ADR-NNNN.

rules.why: The MADR template fixes the status vocabulary; agents read it.
rules.false_positive_control: exact

rules.name: adr-number-collision
rules.statement: two ADR files share a number, or a number lies outside the reserved block of its lane

witness.detail: the two files or the file and the block

messages.text: ADR number {number} is used by {file_a} and {file_b}.
ADR {number} ({file}) lies outside the block {block} reserved for lane {lane}.

rules.why: Parallel lanes collide on numbers unless a tool checks; this design task itself met an allocation mismatch (0095 is allocated to the extractor protocol in ARCHITECTURE.md section 11).
rules.false_positive_control: exact; the reserved blocks are read from docs/adr/README.md

rules.name: accepted-adr-rewritten
rules.statement: accepted ADR whose body digest (adr-body-v1: everything but the Status line) differs from the digest recorded at acceptance

witness.detail: the ADR and both digests

messages.text: ADR {adr} was accepted with body digest {accepted} but now has {current}; supersede it with a new ADR instead.

rules.why: docs/adr/README.md: a record is never rewritten after acceptance. Needs a new hash method adr-body-v1 (proposal to the okf lane) and an acceptance ledger entry (ADR-0094).
rules.false_positive_control: exact given the method; blocked by two dependencies, so phase 3

rules.name: adr-oss-check-missing
rules.statement: ADR lists a custom module but its OSS-check table has no filled row

witness.detail: the ADR and the empty table

messages.text: ADR {adr} adds a custom module but its OSS-check table has no row with a tool, a reason and a replacement path.

rules.why: ADR-0016 (OSS first, adapters not engines) is enforced at the moment a decision is recorded; the template already requires the table.
rules.false_positive_control: exact on the table structure; whether the reason is good is a review question

rules.name: non-posix-or-absolute-path
rules.statement: id or path with a backslash, a drive letter, a leading slash or a .. segment

witness.detail: the path and the offending character class

messages.text: {file} contains path {path} ({problem}); use a repo-relative POSIX path (D-05).

rules.why: ruff analyze graph keys use backslashes on Windows (MEASUREMENT); paths must be normalised at extraction.
rules.false_positive_control: exact

rules.name: nondeterministic-api-use
rules.statement: eijagraph code uses a banned nondeterministic API (wall clock, uuid4, random, hostname, locale, nx.condensation, graphlib order, os.listdir, glob.glob)

witness.detail: the call site

messages.text: {file} line {line} uses {api}: {reason}.

rules.why: Ruff TID251 banned-api flagged 7 of 8 probe sites, including aliased networkx.condensation and attribute access such as datetime.datetime.now (MEASUREMENT, ruff 0.15.7 and 0.16.9, same results); the banned list is generated from this catalogue so rule and configuration cannot drift.
rules.false_positive_control: exact for module members; module bans flag the import, not each use; Path methods are not covered (WV-085)

rules.name: unpinned-extractor-record
rules.statement: extractor_record(E) lacks tool, grammar, python minor or rule fingerprint

witness.detail: the extractor and the missing pin

messages.text: Extractor {extractor} has no {field} in the manifest (D-11).

rules.why: Tool, grammar, Python minor version and rule fingerprint belong in every cache key; without them a cache hit can be wrong (tree-sitter grammar ABIs differ, 14 versus 15, MEASUREMENT).
rules.false_positive_control: exact

rules.name: unsorted-iteration-in-emitter
rules.statement: call to iterdir, glob, rglob, listdir, scandir or walk, or iteration over a set, not directly under sorted(...) in eijagraph code

witness.detail: the call site and the construct

messages.text: {file} line {line}: {construct} is not wrapped in sorted(); its order is not deterministic (D-01, D-09).

rules.why: Ruff's TID251 cannot see Path.iterdir, and PLC0208 flags only iteration over a set literal of literals, not set(xs) or {*xs} (MEASUREMENT, ruff 0.15.7 and 0.16.9, same results); a narrow stdlib ast rule closes that gap and the permutation harness (WV-088) is the real oracle.
rules.false_positive_control: narrow syntactic patterns only; sets used for membership tests are fine; it may miss aliasing, which the harness catches

rules.name: missing-explicit-encoding-or-newline
rules.statement: open, read_text or write_text in eijagraph without encoding, or a text write without newline set to LF

witness.detail: the call site

messages.text: {file} line {line}: {call} without {missing}; use encoding="utf-8" and newline="\n" (D-03).

rules.why: Ruff PLW1514 (preview) flags a missing encoding; it does not flag a missing newline argument (MEASUREMENT, ruff 0.15.7 and 0.16.9, same results), so a small ast check covers newline. Windows cp1252 defaults broke a dossier probe.
rules.false_positive_control: exact for the listed calls

tool_backed.note: preview rule; pin ruff and set preview

rules.name: rebuild-root-mismatch
rules.statement: root hash of build 1 != root hash of build 2 from a clean checkout

witness.detail: the two roots and the first differing view

messages.text: Two clean rebuilds give roots {root_a} and {root_b}; first differing view {view} (D-17).

rules.why: The reproducible-builds acceptance sentence applied to the graph: same inputs, bit-identical outputs.
rules.false_positive_control: exact; the harness is the oracle
rules.not_run_when: POSIX runner unavailable (Windows only measured today)

rules.name: permutation-output-diverged
rules.statement: SARIF bytes differ across file order, rule order, PYTHONHASHSEED, TZ, LC_ALL, CWD, CRLF, threads or non-BMP input

witness.detail: the permutation axis and the first differing byte of the SARIF

messages.text: SARIF output changed under permutation {axis}; first difference at byte {offset} (D-19).

rules.why: The permutation harness requires one distinct output over the whole matrix; a rule that breaks it is a defect in the rule, not in the harness.
rules.false_positive_control: exact for the tested matrix; determinism for all inputs is not claimed

rules.name: hash-method-golden-drift
rules.statement: golden vector of hash method M no longer reproduces, while the method name is unchanged

witness.detail: the golden digest and the recomputed one

messages.text: Hash method {method} produced {actual} for golden input {vector}, expected {expected}; a normalisation change needs a new method name (D-13).

rules.why: Changing a normaliser without renaming it silently re-baselines every link; golden vectors per method catch it (okf ADR-0046: new method name plus full re-baseline).
rules.false_positive_control: exact

rules.name: sarif-profile-violation
rules.statement: SARIF output has a GUID, timestamp, absolute path, machine or account field, unsorted array or missing columnKind

witness.detail: the JSON pointer of the offending element

messages.text: SARIF element {pointer} violates the determinism profile: {problem} (D-22).

rules.why: SARIF 2.1.0 Appendix F lists the non-deterministic elements (result.guid, invocation.startTimeUtc, machine, account, commandLine, absolute paths); the profile forbids them and this rule checks the output.
rules.false_positive_control: exact; the profile is closed

rules.name: suppression-expired
rules.statement: suppression(S, Expiry), Expiry reached under the explicit as-of input, ledger sequence, release or digest

witness.detail: the suppression and its expiry condition

messages.text: Suppression {id} expired: {condition}.
Suppression {id} has a date expiry but no --as-of input was given; it does not suppress.

rules.why: Suppressions expire by ledger sequence, release tag, subject digest or an explicit as-of date; nothing reads the wall clock. An unevaluable expiry fails closed.
rules.false_positive_control: exact; date expiry needs the as-of input recorded in the run

rules.name: rule-without-fixtures
rules.statement: catalogue_rule(R), fewer than the required positive, negative, mutation and golden fixtures

witness.detail: the rule and the fixture kinds found

messages.text: Rule {rule} lacks {missing}: every rule needs positive and negative fixtures, a mutation matrix and a golden SARIF.

rules.why: A rule that cannot fail is worse than no rule (quality ADR-0035); the fixture matrix is derived from the catalogue so nothing is hand-listed.
rules.false_positive_control: exact

rules.name: rule-without-decision-entry
rules.statement: catalogue_rule(R), no decision_entry(R)

witness.detail: the rule

messages.text: Rule {rule} has no ADR-lite entry in graph/rules/decisions.jsonl.

rules.why: Adding a rule is a decision with a cost (false positives, review load); the ADR-lite entry records problem, evidence, alternatives, cost and revisit trigger. Presence only: whether an entry has real content is the promotion gate in graph/rules/check_catalogue.py (a rule that leaves proposed needs alternatives_checked true and its own alternatives text).
rules.false_positive_control: exact

rules.name: forbidden-form-in-prose
rules.statement: prose_token(Doc, Pos, Words), term_form(T, C, F, forbidden), F occurs in Words outside code

witness.detail: the document and the position

messages.text: {document} uses forbidden form {form}; use {replaced_by} (term {term}).

rules.why: Docs, ADRs and OKF pages are read by agents; a forbidden form there re-teaches the wrong word. markdown-it-py's AST excludes code spans and fences.
rules.false_positive_control: markdown AST only, code excluded, exact token match, per-context scope; diff-only gating with the baseline ratchet

rules.name: forbidden-form-in-ui-literal
rules.statement: ui_literal(File, Pos, Text), term_form(T, C, F, forbidden), F occurs in Text

witness.detail: the file and the literal

messages.text: {file} shows {text} containing forbidden form {form}; use {replaced_by}.

rules.why: The static tier of the language check on the UI as written; the rendered tier (WV-033) checks the accessible name the browser computes. Static parsing sees only static literals and says so.
rules.false_positive_control: static-visible only; reported as such, never as complete

rules.name: okf-link-untyped
rules.statement: okf_link(Page1, Page2), no typed declared link between the two concepts

witness.detail: the two pages

messages.text: OKF pages {page_a} and {page_b} link in prose but no typed link joins their concepts; agents cannot tell what the link means.

rules.why: OKF v0.2 links are untyped (the kind is carried by prose) and broken links are tolerated; the typed sidecar carries the kind, and this rule shows where prose links have none.
rules.false_positive_control: exact; note only, because prose links are legitimate navigation

rules.name: ledger-actor-not-human
rules.statement: ledger(Seq, Actor, ...), Actor is not a declared human actor

witness.detail: the ledger entry and its actor

messages.text: Ledger entry {seq} was written by {actor}; only human actors may acknowledge, approve or decide.

rules.why: Agents and providers never approve or apply; the ledger's actor grammar is defined by ADR-0094 (assumed human:<id> as in the okf lane). A declared actor is not identity: integrity rests on git history.
rules.false_positive_control: exact against the declared actor registry; not a sandbox against an agent with OS write access

rules.name: protected-policy-digest-mismatch
rules.statement: protected_file(P, D), approved_digest(P, A), D != A

witness.detail: the path, its digest and the owner-approved digest

messages.text: {path} has digest {current} but the owner approved {approved}; severity, maturity, policy and baseline changes need an owner ledger entry.

rules.why: Agents may not change protected policy to make a gate pass; the catalogue's severity and maturity fields, the coverage and layer policy, the suppression ledger and the baseline are protected paths pinned by owner-approved digest.
rules.false_positive_control: exact; an agent with OS write access can still edit the ledger, which git history and review reveal

fix.what: clearing is a human ledger act (ADR-0094); an agent may propose a review summary only

rules.name: diagram-label-drift
rules.statement: view_fact(Diagram, Id, label, L), names(Id, T), L not in forms(T)

witness.detail: the diagram element and the term forms

messages.text: Diagram element {element} is labelled {label}, which is not a form of term {term}.

rules.why: Diagrams are generated from the model, so a label that is not a registered form means the generator or the registry drifted.
rules.false_positive_control: exact over generated labels; hand-drawn views are get-only and not linted here

rules.name: test-without-requirement
rules.statement: node.test(N), count(covered_link of kind verifies, outgoing, N) < 1

witness.detail: the closed-world scope: node, link kind, side, the links seen and their statuses

messages.text: Test {node} verifies {count} requirements, invariants or workflow elements (needs {min}).

rules.why: A test that verifies no requirement, invariant or workflow element has no stated purpose (orphan: test without requirement). Note-level until the coverage policy lists the exempt helper tests.
rules.false_positive_control: policy-limited: infrastructure tests are declared exempt in coverage_policy, not skipped inline
rules.metamodel: proposed to the metamodel lane (verifies obligation, out side, on test)
